incidents.vector: Hackers breached the servers of Japan's largest refrigerated-logistics operator, forcing it to disconnect key systems to contain the intrusion.
incidents.impact: Frozen and refrigerated shipments across 140 distribution centers were halted, leaving all 1,300+ KFC Japan outlets short of ingredients and causing shortages at major retailers and restaurant chains; some affected servers held personal data still under investigation.

incidents.victim: Users across the U.S. and Europe
incidents.vector: A Russian-speaking crew used ClickFix social engineering and trojanized software installers (MobaXterm, Zoom, WebEx, DBeaver) to deploy the Python-based 'Starland' RAT and a bespoke PowerShell C2 implant.
incidents.impact: The malware steals browser credentials and cryptocurrency wallets and enables follow-on payloads (CastleStealer, Remcos); Cisco Talos reports predominant impact in the U.S. with additional victims in Germany, Romania and Venezuela.

incidents.vector: Attackers chained two zero-days (CVE-2026-15409 and CVE-2026-15410) in SonicWall SMA1000 appliances to move from no access to full system compromise, exploiting them roughly three weeks before patches shipped.
incidents.impact: Rapid7 observed active exploitation from June 22 with ransomware as the likely goal; CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and SonicWall urged immediate patching and compromise hunting.

incidents.vector: Data-extortion group FulcrumSec exploited weak access controls to exfiltrate about 1.3TB of data and used AI agents to analyze stolen private drug-discovery models.
incidents.impact: The group claims to have taken five undisclosed drug programs and RNA-delivery IP it says could save competitors 3-5 years of development, and issued a $25M ransom demand while publicly disparaging the company's security.

incidents.vector: Three St. Petersburg-based Russian nationals allegedly ran bulletproof hosting providers Media Land and ML.Cloud that supplied infrastructure for malware, ransomware, phishing and DDoS attacks.
incidents.impact: DOJ unsealed indictments tied to attacks causing over $62M in losses across 21 states and several countries; the State Department offered up to $10M for information as prior U.S., UK and Australian sanctions remain in force.

incidents.vector: Russian FSB Center 16 actors scan for poorly configured networking devices, abusing weak or default SNMP community strings and Cisco Smart Install to copy router configurations via TFTP to actor-controlled servers.
incidents.impact: A joint advisory from NSA, CISA, FBI, ASD and 15+ allied agencies warned of decade-plus opportunistic compromise of energy, telecom, government, financial and healthcare infrastructure routers and urged SNMPv3 and device hardening.

incidents.vector: Threat actors actively exploited SharePoint flaws (CVE-2026-56164, CVE-2026-32201 and CVE-2026-45659) to achieve remote code execution and steal IIS machine keys for persistence.
incidents.impact: CISA urged emergency hardening as attackers deploy webshells and malware; Microsoft also flagged an actively exploited AD FS privilege-escalation zero-day (CVE-2026-56155) within a record 622-CVE Patch Tuesday.

incidents.vector: Attackers pushed malicious commits to unprotected pre-production release branches of four AsyncAPI GitHub repos, triggering CI/CD workflows that harvested NPM_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN secrets and published five trojanized npm packages.
incidents.impact: The 'miasma-train-p1' packages deploy a descendant of the Miasma RAT that steals developer, cloud, SSH and CI/CD credentials and establishes persistence using IPFS-hosted payloads and blockchain-based command-and-control fallback.

incidents.victim: Lidl online shop customers (Germany, Belgium, Netherlands)
incidents.vector: Attackers accessed and exfiltrated part of a customer database maintained by one of Lidl's third-party IT service providers.
incidents.impact: Stolen data includes names, phone numbers, email addresses and dates of birth; Lidl said no passwords or payment data were exposed but warned customers of phishing and identity-theft risk and filed a criminal complaint.

incidents.vector: Attackers gained access to Nayax systems and exfiltrated a backup of scanned documents and payment transaction records before making an extortion demand.
incidents.impact: The Israeli payments firm told the SEC its production systems were unaffected and safeguarded funds untouched; exposed records excluded sensitive authentication data, and the board refused to pay the criminal extortion demand.

incidents.victim: U.S. businesses, hospitals, financial firms and municipalities
incidents.vector: First VPN Service (1VPNS) sold anonymity infrastructure that ransomware operators used to hide attack origins, deploy malware and manage exfiltrated data.
incidents.impact: The U.S. Treasury and UK sanctioned 1VPNS and its alleged Ukrainian administrator, plus a Belarusian national selling malware 'cryptors'; Europol had earlier arrested the service's administrator in a May sting.

incidents.victim: ~2 million compromised home devices (smart TVs, streaming boxes)
incidents.vector: The NetNut residential-proxy service (a.k.a. the Popa botnet) enrolled home devices as always-on proxy exit nodes via malicious SDKs bundled into apps and devices.
incidents.impact: The FBI, Google and Lumen seized hundreds of NetNut domains and degraded the ~2M-device network used to mask cybercriminal and espionage traffic; Google saw 316 distinct threat clusters using its exit nodes in a single week.

incidents.victim: Internet-connected cameras across NATO, EU and Ukraine
incidents.vector: At least one Russian intelligence service scanned for internet-exposed IP cameras, exploited default passwords and outdated firmware, then used image-recognition software to identify military vehicles and cargo.
incidents.impact: Dutch intelligence services (AIVD/MIVD) warned the campaign collects NATO military-logistics and weapons-shipment intelligence; in Ukraine, hacked cameras have helped locate soldiers to support lethal strikes.
